item.title: Hungarian Central Banker Touts Benefits of Joining Euro Area
item.description: Hungary’s central bank renewed its support for the government’s efforts to meet conditions for joining the euro area, saying it would benefit the economy.

item.title: Apple Explores Apple Watch Shake-Up; Company Prepares for September iPhone Event
item.description: Also: The company’s big iPhone event approaches.

item.title: Behind Bessent Moves, Wall Street Sees Sign of Bond-Market Angst
item.description: Wall Street traders and strategists say US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is sending fresh signals that he’s eager to keep bond yields from spiking higher.

item.title: Leveraged ETF Boom Amps Up Wall Street Intraday Momentum Plays
item.description: The leveraged ETF boom is creating new ways to profit from sudden bursts of volatility in tech stocks.

item.title: Turkey Resumes Black Sea Ship Transits Via Straits After Delays
item.description: Turkey resumed allowing ships to transit its straits on the way to the Black Sea, following unexplained delays for some vessels amid heightened security risks in the area.

item.title: Barrick Chairman's Planned Overhaul Meets Investor Backlash
item.description: John Thornton appeared ready last year to step down as chairman of Barrick Mining Corp. after a turbulent 12-year tenure. Instead, he seized control from his long-time CEO and is now driving a reinvention of one of the world’s largest gold producers.

item.title: Currency Defense Gets Makeover as Emerging Asia Guards Reserves
item.description: Central banks in emerging Asia are increasingly finding ways to support their currencies without dipping into foreign-exchange reserves, as recurring Middle East tensions and the prospect of higher-for-longer US interest rates keep policymakers on edge.

item.title: China AI Chip Designer Moore Threads Plans Hong Kong Listing
item.description: Artificial intelligence chipmaker Moore Threads Technology Co. said it plans to list in Hong Kong at an “appropriate time” after its shares have surged more than 420% since their Shanghai debut last year.

item.title: Romania Extends Reactor Output by Nine Days After Danube Blasts
item.description: Romania can keep the second nuclear reactor at its Cernavoda plant in operation for at least nine more days after explosive works on the Danube led to an increase in the flow of the river by 4cm (1.6 inches).

item.title: Europe’s Hot Stock Markets Are Creating a Buzz Among Investors
item.description: Europe’s stock market is firing on all cylinders and drawing money managers who say this rally will be more durable than just another short-term trade.

item.title: China Issues Red Alert, Airports Cancel Flights as Typhoon Nears
item.description: China issued its highest storm alert in preparation for approaching Typhoon Dolphin as more than 1,000 flights were canceled and some rail services were suspended.

item.title: China’s Inflation Cools as Iran War Oil Shock Starts to Ease
item.description: China’s factory-gate inflation eased for the first time since the Iran war broke out in late February while consumer prices also decelerated, in another sign that cost pressures from the oil shock are starting to fade.

item.title: Korea Volatility Spike Ebbs as Leveraged Trades Are Flushed Out
item.description: The most extreme phase of South Korea’s stock-market turmoil may be over after a historic selloff flushed out leveraged positions and regulatory curbs sent trading in some of the riskiest products plunging.

item.title: US CPI to Show Inflationary Pressures Cooling Some
item.description: Prices paid by US consumers probably inched up marginally last month after falling for the first time in six years, a welcome tempering in recent war-driven inflationary pressures.

item.title: Private Credit Squeezed By Bank Refinancings: Credit Weekly
item.description: Highly-indebted companies are increasingly ditching private credit loans for cheaper capital in the bank loan market, a shift underscoring the stark realities of higher-for-longer interest rates.

item.title: A Tough Week for Crypto Has Fans Downing Drinks at a Bitcoin Bar
item.description: It was a tough week for crypto, but a good time to get a drink by Thursday evening.

item.title: Fintech That Soared on Trump Sells Core Business for $12 Million
item.description: A virtually unknown fintech that catapulted into the headlines and cracked a $1 billion market value after signing a deal with the Trump family’s crypto platform last year has sold its core business for about $12 million.

item.title: Singapore to Ensure AI Helps Workers Worried About Jobs, PM Says
item.description: Singapore is benefitting from the rapid growth of artificial intelligence and the government is making use of the technology to ensure higher productivity and better jobs for workers who are worried about their livelihoods, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said.

item.title: How AI Is Triggering a Surge in American Imports: New Economy
item.description: Deep-pocketed tech firms racing to build data centers have largely gotten a pass from Trump’s protectionism.

item.title: World Economy Latest: US Employment Declines Unexpectedly
item.description: A surprise drop in US payrolls renewed worries about the job market in the world’s largest economy, suggesting employers are growing cautious amid rising prices and fallout from the Iran war.

item.title: Zimbabwe to Cap Gold-Buying Support at $300 Million This Year
item.description: Zimbabwe said it will cap government support for buying gold at $300 million this year and review the scheme in the 2027 national budget, according to a letter from top economic officials to the International Monetary Fund.

item.title: Zelenskyy Makes Debut Trip to Serbia as Russian Influence Wanes
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is making a landmark first visit on Saturday to Serbia, the Balkan country whose leader has been scaling back once-close ties with Russia.

item.title: Kyiv Struck as Ukraine Targets Russian Refineries, Shadow Fleet
item.description: A fire was sparked at Russia’s Ilsky oil refinery in the southern Krasnodar region by Ukrainian drone debris, injuring five people, the regional task force said on Saturday, as Russia and Ukraine exchanged overnight attacks including a large-scale missile barrage on Kyiv.

item.title: Burnham’s Fiscal ‘Flexibility’ Could Backfire, Officials Fear
item.description: UK Treasury officials are concerned that the prime minister’s talk of using “flexibility” within the fiscal rules to ramp up investment could backfire by destabilizing financial markets, according to people familiar with the thinking.

item.title: WuXi AppTec Gets Temporary Reprieve of Chinese Military Label
item.description: A US judge blocked the Defense Department from enforcing its designation of WuXi AppTec Co. as a Chinese military company, granting temporary relief to the major pharmaceutical contractor.

item.title: War Brings Winter of Discontent for the World’s Workhorse Fuel
item.description: A diesel squeeze spurred by wars in the Middle East and Ukraine is setting the stage for an even worse crunch as demand rises ahead of the Northern Hemisphere winter.

item.title: Situational Awareness’s Mystery Investment Was to Source Foundry
item.description: A mystery $400 million investment made by Situational Awareness just days after the hedge fund was on the brink of collapse was to chip manufacturing startup Source Foundry, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Union Workers Strike at BHP’s Port Hedland Iron Ore Export Hub
item.description: Unionized workers at BHP Group’s Port Hedland iron ore export hub in Western Australia have started rolling 24-hour strikes, escalating a pay dispute ahead of further meetings with the company.

item.title: Canada’s PSP Is Said to Mull $1.5 Billion Sale of Roads in India
item.description: The Public Sector Pension Investment Board is exploring options for its roads in India, including a sale, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: New Zealand Slaps New Sanctions Against Russia After US Move
item.description: New Zealand announced more sanctions targeting individuals and entities supporting Russia’s war against Ukraine, following the passage of a new bill in the US Senate targeting the country’s oil and gas revenues.
